reasoning: Focused UI change to offset map camera position. Requires modifying 1-2 files in the UI layer with well-documented Google Maps camera APIs. No new dependencies, no infrastructure changes, and the pattern (camera offset for navigation mode) is standard in mapping applications.

scope.notes: Primary change in LiveRideScreen.kt (3 camera update locations). May add a helper function for offset calculation. LocationMarker.kt unchanged - it renders at GPS location which is correct.

integrations.notes: Using existing Google Maps Android SDK (com.google.maps.android.compose). Camera offset via CameraUpdateFactory is well-documented standard API.

infrastructure.notes: Pure UI layer change. No backend, database, or configuration changes required.

knowledge.notes: Codebase already uses Google Maps camera APIs extensively (CameraUpdateFactory.newLatLngZoom, CameraPosition). The offset calculation (shift camera target north based on zoom/screen) follows standard navigation app patterns.

concerns: Need to test offset calculation at different zoom levels
Portrait vs landscape orientation may need different offsets
Should preserve smooth animation during location updates
risk.notes: Purely visual change with no security implications. Easy to verify by visual inspection. Rollback is trivial.

implementation_hints.current_behavior: Camera centers on user location using CameraUpdateFactory.newLatLngZoom(location, 17f) at 3 locations in LiveRideScreen.kt (lines 113, 517, 583)
implementation_hints.target_behavior: Camera targets a point north of user location so rider arrow appears in lower ~1/3 of screen, providing more forward visibility
implementation_hints.approach: Calculate offset latitude based on zoom level - at zoom 17f, approximately 0.001-0.002 degrees north offset to position user in lower third

validation_recommendations.reasoning: Simple UI positioning change with no security implications. Visual verification is primary validation. Unit test for offset calculation if helper function is created. No E2E needed for camera positioning.
